subject: Override Questions Six, Seven, and Eight
overview: Medford Happenings broadcast a presentation by City Councilor George Scarpelli addressing the city's upcoming Proposition 2 1/2 ballot override and debt exclusion measures. Scarpelli argued against Questions 6, 7, and 8, recommending instead the use of municipal free cash reserves and alternative revenue sources.

items.title: Introduction
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduces the episode featuring a recorded presentation by City Councilor George Scarpelli opposing the city's upcoming ballot questions.

items.title: Question 6: Fire Station Debt Exclusion
items.summary: Scarpelli outlines ballot Question 6 regarding a debt exclusion to construct a new fire station headquarters at 120 Main Street and urges residents to vote against it.

items.title: Question 7: School Operations and Infrastructure Override
items.summary: Scarpelli reviews Question 7 for funding school operations and public works infrastructure, arguing that existing free cash reserves should be utilized rather than a tax increase.

items.title: Question 8: Vocational, Arts, and Compensation Override
items.summary: Scarpelli discusses Question 8 regarding expanded vocational programming, arts access, and staff compensation, asserting that the cost does not justify an override.

items.title: Municipal Finances, Free Cash, and Council Procedures
items.summary: Scarpelli reviews previous city council debates regarding Rule 21 and the financial task force, citing Somerville's historic revenue planning and advocating to address deficits through Medford's reported $34 million in free cash.

items.title: Campaign Strategy and Tax Impact Discussion
items.summary: Scarpelli outlines volunteer canvassing and lawn sign distribution efforts while warning of potential tax and rent burdens on senior citizens and tenants.

items.title: Program Closing
items.summary: Petrella closes the broadcast and provides station viewing and contact details.
